reusable_patterns.pattern: Keep calculation separate from persistence. A desk pass clones input state, produces records, and commits the result under a writer lock. Reuse this for zero-strategy tasks and observations.

Account equity is cash plus marked open holdings. Buying removes full purchase cost; selling returns proceeds; paper fills retain whether they used bid/ask or a scheduled cost. Make these distinctions explicit in the new ledger.

Paper and Sim expose the same account, positions, orders, order lookup, submit, cancel, price and market-clock methods. The replay adapter owns simulated cash/positions; the paper adapter reads the broker account. Reuse the interface boundary with an initially disabled order capability.

The quant ledger has sequential hashes and fsync; config/playbook content hashes are pinned in records and checked before use. Every runtime record has phase, mode and playbook version. Reuse provenance for task inputs, agent configuration and tool decisions, without copying trading rules.

Generate deterministic client order IDs, persist the intent before submit, look up an ambiguous submission by that ID, and adopt broker orders on restart. Settle intents only after a durable state save. This is the strongest reusable external-action pattern.

Refresh fill status, compare broker quantities with desk quantities, adopt known orphan orders, and block symbols with unmanaged holdings/orders or mismatches. Separate expected state, observed state and reconciliation exceptions.

Write a temporary state file, flush/fsync, replace it, and fsync the directory. Persist records and partial-pass state even when a pass raises. Reuse atomic snapshots for single-host operation or implement the equivalent in a transactional database.

Midna starts a deterministic five-minute equity loop, prevents overlapping ticks, checks child ownership and heartbeat age, and restarts with exponential backoff. Reuse scheduling independently of the frontend.

Midna persists an attempt before watch/pass execution and marks the slot complete only after both succeed. Quant adds bounded retries, done/failed records, and a ledger run_end proof; process presence alone does not count as successful work. Reuse this for scheduled agent tasks.

Use one writer and separate read-only views, observers and publishers. Midna public GETs expose views while passes require an explicit action; the quant publisher reads desk state and has its own single-instance loop.

Daily contextual journal entries and unfrozen memory are separate from frozen runtime configuration. The source explicitly treats contextual notes as review inputs rather than authority to alter execution. Preserve this separation for agent-generated research and operations notes.
A rerun close replaces the existing trading-date P&L row rather than appending duplicates; non-trading dates are skipped. Keep daily snapshots distinct from immutable fill events.

operational_limits.finding: The inspected runtime paths implement deterministic scheduled functions and named seat messages. They do not include LLM calls, agent delegation, durable generic task queues, task leases, tool traces or agent checkpoints. The new agent runtime requires these components. Journal prose and role labels are not evidence of an autonomous worker.

The separate Midna crypto floor applies exits on action handling and privately polls POST tick every nine seconds. Its store serializes mutations with an in-process Promise queue. This is unsuitable as the ownership/scheduling mechanism for unattended multi-worker agents; no independent crypto floor loop was identified in the inspected supervisor.
operational_limits.confidence: high for source behavior; scoped absence

operational_limits.finding: Midna equity has exclusive-file locks with PID/mtime heartbeat and staged next-state recovery; its writes do not fsync and its schedule journal is rewritten directly. These provide a useful single-host model, not transactional multi-worker storage or a distributed lease. Prefer a database transaction plus explicit task lease for the new desk.

Quant appends the event batch and then saves state in separate files. Intent recovery covers external order ambiguity, but the code does not make the ledger batch and state update one atomic transaction. Reuse the write-ahead intent concept with a transactional ledger/state/outbox for a new multi-worker runtime.

Quant reads cumulative filled_qty and cumulative filled_avg_price, then adds only new_qty times that cumulative average to realized P&L. If an exit order fills at changing prices across polls, this does not equal the incremental fill proceeds. A new ledger should use broker fill events or delta(cumulative_qty * cumulative_average_price), with decimal money amounts. This is a static arithmetic observation; no runtime outcomes were recomputed.
operational_limits.confidence: high for source formula, no production impact measured

operational_limits.finding: The quant user-space watchdog starts missing schedulers and warns about a stale heartbeat of an existing process without restarting it. It dies with the box and uses deployment-specific workspace/scratch paths. A new desk needs explicit process/host lifecycle ownership and a policy for stalled workers.

Quant daily_pnl.csv stores cumulative realized_usd summed over all positions and broker account equity. Preserve the cumulative label and account scope; do not treat the realized_usd field as that day's realized profit. Paper/sim/research-valued accounts also need separate source and price-time labels.
